sections.h2: Who sends the tax bill and keeps the parcel maps in Bertie County?
sections.html:
Tax Collections and Tax Mapping is one department inside the county office building at 106 Dundee Street in Windsor. The tax line, (252) 794-5310, takes bill and payment questions. The mapping line, (252) 794-5311, covers parcels, maps and ownership by street address.

The county website's Online Services menu links to a tax bill payment page and a real property search. The register of deeds indexes by name only, so a buyer or seller who starts with an address should start with the mapping line.

  • Bills and payments: (252) 794-5310
  • Parcels, maps and address lookups: (252) 794-5311
  • Recording and deed indexes: our Bertie County register of deeds page

sections.h2: What kind of county is Bertie, and how does that affect a sale?
sections.html:
Bertie covers 741 square miles of farm and timber land, and Windsor, established in 1766, has been the county seat since 1774. Eight towns are incorporated: Askewville, Aulander, Colerain, Kelford, Lewiston-Woodville, Powellsville, Roxobel and Windsor. The 2020 census counted 17,934 people countywide and 3,582 in Windsor.

Fertile uplands and lowlands share the county with large swamps called pocosins, and timber, livestock and broiler chickens anchor the economy. QuickFacts shows a shrinking population: 17,086 in mid-2025 against 17,933 in the April 2020 base.

Of 9,116 housing units, 72.7% sit in the Census's owner-occupied rate. The typical value for 2020 to 2024 was $98,500, compared with $332,700 for the country, and builders pulled 32 permits in 2025. At that price level a back-tax bill is a large slice of any sale, so clear the tax record before you list. Median household income is $48,750 for 2020 to 2024, and 20.1% of residents live in poverty.

Land records here carry a notice required by state law: any tract within half a mile of a farm in a voluntary agricultural district is flagged, so a buyer researching title sees the farm next door.

sections.h2: When was Bertie County last revalued, and when is the next one?
sections.html:
The last reappraisal took effect January 1, 2020, and NCDOR's schedule puts the next in 2028. State law sets an eight-year ceiling and fixes values at January 1 of the reappraisal year.

In the years between, a value shifts mainly with building, demolition or rezoning. A house priced off 2020 schedules can end up well above or below what a buyer will pay now. The tax department posts a locational sales report for each year from 2012 through 2025. Read the one for your area, and request your property record card, before you argue a value.

Neighboring counties are on different clocks, as the table below shows, so a Bertie seller comparing rates with a Hertford or Martin listing is looking at values from different years. Since the lien runs from the January 1 listing date, an inflated number costs money on every bill until 2028 arrives.

sections.h2: How does the Bertie County tax rate compare with nearby counties?
sections.html:

sections.h2: What does late payment of a Bertie County tax bill cost?
sections.html:
Bills fall due September 1. Interest stays off through January 5, then 2% attaches on January 6, and each month or part of a month after February 1 adds another three-fourths of a percent. A postmark counts for mailed checks.

An unpaid bill can lead to a court action that mirrors a mortgage foreclosure, with a public sale at the courthouse door and a deposit of up to 20% from the high bidder. Until the court confirms that sale, the owner can still redeem by paying taxes, penalties, interest and costs, so closing a sale of the house inside that window ends the matter.

Bertie also sells county-owned parcels by the upset bid method under G.S. 160A-269. An offer comes with a 5% deposit, a notice runs in the newspaper, and anyone can top the offer within 10 days by 10% of the first $1,000 plus 5% of the rest. The board can reject any offer.

sections.h2: Which tax relief can a Bertie County homeowner claim?
sections.html:
Three state programs reduce the tax on a permanent residence, and they share a single application. Only one can apply to an owner. Bertie's tax page also hosts a physician certificate form for disability claims a motor vehicle exemption form and a general exemption application.

Relief matters here because QuickFacts counts 26.9% of residents as 65 or older, so the elderly exclusion and the circuit breaker can reach a large share of owners. Each owner still has to meet the income test on the application.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: shields the larger of $25,000 or half the appraised value of a home owned by someone 65 or older, or totally and permanently disabled. NCDOR prints $38,800 as the 2026 income cap.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: shields the first $45,000 and asks nothing about age or income. A service-connected total and permanent disability qualifies, and so can an unmarried surviving spouse.
  • Circuit breaker: limits yearly tax to 4% of income, or 5% when income runs up to 150% of the cap, with the excess deferred as a lien.

File with the county assessor. January is the usual window, but a filing is accepted through June 1 ahead of the tax year.

sections.h2: What does a Bertie County seller owe on the tax side at closing?
sections.html:
The seller's proceeds cover back and current bills. Obtain a written payoff from the tax office so the closing attorney works from a firm number.

A circuit breaker owner faces one more charge: a transfer is a disqualifying event, and the deferred amounts for the last three years come due with interest.

The state deed tax is also the seller's, at $1.00 per $500 or fraction thereof of the price, paid at the register of deeds before recording. Bertie's own recording resolution requires a return name and address and the buyer's permanent mailing address on each instrument's face.

Inherited title, tenants and deferred repairs leave all of this unchanged. A financed buyer and a cash buyer trigger the same payoffs, and an as-is sale does not lift a lien before closing.

faqs.q: What is the Bertie County tax office phone number?
faqs.a: Bills and payments go through (252) 794-5310. For parcel maps and who owns an address, use (252) 794-5311.

faqs.q: When is Bertie County scheduled to reappraise next?
faqs.a: NCDOR lists 2028. The most recent reappraisal took effect January 1, 2020, and no county may go beyond eight years.

faqs.q: What is the cutoff to challenge a Bertie County value?
faqs.a: The cutoff is the date the county board of equalization and review adjourns, or 15 days after its notice is mailed when that notice went out with under 15 days left. The board starts between the first Monday in April and the first Monday in May and mails its ruling within 30 days. A Property Tax Commission appeal must be filed within 30 days of that mailing.

faqs.q: Do unpaid taxes come out of my sale proceeds in Bertie County?
faqs.a: Yes, closing pays any unpaid balance out of the proceeds. Ask the tax office for the figure in writing first.

faqs.q: Can a Bertie County home with delinquent taxes be sold?
faqs.a: Yes, provided the price covers the lien, interest and costs. If a foreclosure is already filed, the closing needs to happen before the court confirms the sale.
